title: 3Sum Smaller
summary: Given an array of n integers named nums and an integer target, determine the count of unique triplets (i, j, k) where i, j, and k are indices such that 0 <= i < j < k < n, and the sum of nums[i], nums[j], and nums[k] is less than the target.
statement: Given an array of n integers named nums and an integer target, determine the count of unique triplets (i, j, k) where i, j, and k are indices such that 0 <= i < j < k < n, and the sum of nums[i], nums[j], and nums[k] is less than the target.
constraints: nums contains 0–3500 integers from -100 through 100; target is from -100 through 100. The answer is guaranteed to fit within 10^9.
Count triples of distinct indices i<j<k whose three values sum to strictly less than target. Equal values at different indices form distinct triples.
hints: Sort first so moving one pointer changes the sum predictably.
Fix the first index. If left+middle+right is below target, every index from middle+1 through right also works with that left and middle.
Add right-middle and advance middle on a qualifying sum; otherwise decrement right.
The condition is strictly less than target, and duplicate values still represent separate index choices.
editorial: For each fixed first value, two pointers cover the remaining pairs. When the largest current right value still makes a small enough sum, all right-middle choices from the current interval qualify, so they are counted together. Otherwise only a smaller right value can help. The independent oracle enumerates every three-index combination.

tests.explanation: The qualifying index triples have values (-2,0,1) and (-2,0,3), so the count is 2.
The smallest three-value sum is -1 from (-2,0,1), and it is the only sum strictly below 0, so the count is 1.
